title: What are nakshatra padas? The 108 quarters explained | Ask Tota
description: Each nakshatra splits into four padas of 3 degrees 20 minutes, 108 in all. How padas map to the navamsa, set your name syllable, and refine a reading.
og_description: 27 nakshatras times 4 padas is 108, which is also 12 signs times 9 navamsas. Why that is not a coincidence, and what your pada adds.
h1: nakshatra padas are the 108 quarters that sharpen ur birth star
dek: ur nakshatra is one of twenty-seven. ur pada is one of a hundred and eight. it is the quarter of the nakshatra ur moon sat in, it decides ur navamsa sign and ur traditional name syllable, and it is where the zodiac's two grids lock together.
card_title: nakshatra padas are the 108 quarters that sharpen ur birth star
card_dek: four quarters per nakshatra, 108 in all. they set ur navamsa sign and ur name syllable, and they are where the zodiac's two grids meet.
llms_desc: what nakshatra padas (charans) are, why 27 nakshatras times 4 padas equals 12 signs times 9 navamsas, how each pada maps to a navamsa sign, the purushartha pattern, vargottama padas, gandanta, and how padas give the traditional first syllable of a name.

faq.a: a quarter of a nakshatra. each nakshatra is 13 degrees 20 minutes wide and splits into four padas of 3 degrees 20 minutes each. ur birth pada is the quarter the moon was in when u were born.
108. there are 27 nakshatras and each has 4 padas. 108 is also 12 signs times 9 navamsas, which is why padas and the navamsa chart line up exactly.

faq.q: what is the difference between pada and charan?
faq.a: nothing. charan, or charana, is another word for pada. both mean foot or quarter.

faq.q: how do i find my nakshatra pada?
faq.a: u need ur moon's exact degree, which needs ur birth date, time and place. divide the moon's position within its nakshatra by 3 degrees 20 minutes. any vedic chart tool will print the pada next to the nakshatra.

faq.q: how are padas related to the navamsa chart?
faq.a: each pada is exactly one navamsa. the first pada of ashwini is the aries navamsa, the second is taurus, and so on through the zodiac nine times. so ur moon's pada tells u ur moon's navamsa sign directly.

faq.q: how do padas decide baby names?
faq.a: each of the 108 padas has a traditional syllable. ashwini's four padas are chu, che, cho and la, for example. the naming tradition, namakarana, starts the child's name with the syllable of the moon's birth pada.

none is best in general. some are given special notice: vargottama padas, where a planet's sign and navamsa match, are read as strong, and gandanta padas at water to fire sign junctions are read as sensitive.

a planet in the same sign in the rashi chart and the navamsa. it happens in the first pada of a movable sign, the middle navamsa of a fixed sign, and the last of a dual sign. it is traditionally read as strengthening the planet.

faq.q: what does each pada number mean?
faq.a: a common reading links each pada to a purushartha by the element of its navamsa sign: fire with dharma, earth with artha, air with kama and water with moksha. in ashwini that gives pada 1 dharma, 2 artha, 3 kama, 4 moksha.

the knot where a water sign ends and a fire sign begins: the last pada of ashlesha, jyeshtha and revati and the first pada of magha, mula and ashwini. traditional astrology treats a moon or lagna there as needing extra care in reading.

faq.q: does my pada change my dasha?
faq.a: not the mahadasha lord, which comes from the nakshatra. but the exact position inside the nakshatra, which the pada roughly shows, sets how much of the first dasha was left at birth.

faq.q: do padas matter for kundli matching?
faq.a: the ashtakoota system works mainly from the nakshatra and moon sign. padas come in for specific checks, such as some traditions softening nadi dosha when the two moons are in the same nakshatra but different padas.
